title: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Samuel 30](/bible/1-samuel/30)

**[1 Samuel 30:1-6](/bible/1-samuel/30#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/30#v1)</sup> And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/30#v2)</sup> And had taken the women captives, that were therein: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away, and went on their way.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/30#v3)</sup> So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-samuel/30#v4)</sup> Then David and the people that were with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/30#v5)</sup> And David’s two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/30#v6)</sup> And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.

- While David and his men were away with Achish, the Amalekites invaded the south and Ziklag, smote Ziklag and burned it with fire, and carried the women captive; they slew not any, great or small, but carried them away. David and his men came to the city on the third day, found it burned, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive; they lifted up their voice and wept until they had no more power to weep.
- David's two wives were taken, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. David was greatly distressed, for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and his daughters; but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.
- Notice how this connects to yesterday's reading in chapter 27. Achish had given David Ziklag, and David and his men had gone up and invaded the Amalekites and the other old inhabitants of the land, leaving neither man nor woman alive. Now the Amalekites came back and smote Ziklag the same way, taking David's wives and the families of his men while they were gone up with Achish.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Samuel 27:5-6](/bible/1-samuel/27#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/27#v5)</sup> And David said unto Achish, If I have now found grace in thine eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee?
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/27#v6)</sup> Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.

    David asked Achish for a place in some town in the country, and Achish gave him Ziklag that day; wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.
  - **[1 Samuel 27:8-9](/bible/1-samuel/27#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/27#v8)</sup> And David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/27#v9)</sup> And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel, and returned, and came to Achish.

    David and his men had invaded the Geshurites, the Gezrites, and the Amalekites, and smote the land, leaving neither man nor woman alive; this is the raid the Amalekites answered at Ziklag.

**[1 Samuel 30:7-8](/bible/1-samuel/30#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/30#v7)</sup> And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/30#v8)</sup> And David enquired at the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.

- David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, Bring hither the ephod, and David inquired at the Lord: shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? The answer came, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
- David sought the Lord first and asked whether this thing was so before he moved; the Lord said go down, and you will recover.

**[1 Samuel 30:9-10](/bible/1-samuel/30#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/30#v9)</sup> So David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-samuel/30#v10)</sup> But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.

- David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed. David pursued with four hundred men, for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.

**[1 Samuel 30:11-15](/bible/1-samuel/30#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/1-samuel/30#v11)</sup> And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-samuel/30#v12)</sup> And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any water, three days and three nights.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-samuel/30#v13)</sup> And David said unto him, To whom belongest thou? and whence art thou? And he said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days agone I fell sick.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-samuel/30#v14)</sup> We made an invasion upon the south of the Cherethites, and upon the coast which belongeth to Judah, and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-samuel/30#v15)</sup> And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear unto me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.

- They found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David; they gave him bread, water, a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins, and when he had eaten his spirit came again to him, for he had eaten no bread nor drunk any water three days and three nights.
- A sidebar worth saying: this man was faint because he had gone without food three days and three nights. Some of our people are like that after fasting one day on the last Friday of the month; we have got to check our spirits.
- He was a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite, left behind because he fell sick three days before; his company had invaded the south of the Cherethites, the coast of Judah, and the south of Caleb, and burned Ziklag with fire. David asked, Canst thou bring me down to this company? He answered, Swear unto me by God that thou wilt neither kill me nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.

**[1 Samuel 30:16-20](/bible/1-samuel/30#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/1-samuel/30#v16)</sup> And when he had brought him down, behold, they were spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-samuel/30#v17)</sup> And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, which rode upon camels, and fled.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-samuel/30#v18)</sup> And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/30#v19)</sup> And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any thing that they had taken to them: David recovered all.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/30#v20)</sup> And David took all the flocks and the herds, which they drave before those other cattle, and said, This is David’s spoil.

- When he had brought him down, behold, the Amalekites were spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking and dancing because of all the great spoil they had taken out of the land of the Philistines and out of the land of Judah.
- David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day, and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men which rode upon camels and fled.
- David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away, and rescued his two wives; there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil nor any thing that they had taken. David took all the flocks and the herds, and they said, This is David's spoil.

**[1 Samuel 30:21-25](/bible/1-samuel/30#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/1-samuel/30#v21)</sup> And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that were with him: and when David came near to the people, he saluted them.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-samuel/30#v22)</sup> Then answered all the wicked men and men of Belial, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them ought of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away, and depart.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-samuel/30#v23)</sup> Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-samuel/30#v24)</sup> For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-samuel/30#v25)</sup> And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.

- When David came back to the two hundred men at the brook Besor, all the wicked men and men of Belial among those that went with David said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them ought of the spoil that we have recovered, save every man his wife and his children. Notice these were David's own men, yet the scripture calls them wicked men and men of Belial; David called that thinking of the devil, saying they had the devil on them for even thinking like that.
- That is the same spirit a lot of our people have today: I went down there, my hands got me this, you have got to get your own. David said, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.
- The ruling: as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff; they shall part alike. Those that went down into the battle split the spoil with those that stayed behind, and from that day forward David made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.

**[1 Samuel 30:26-31](/bible/1-samuel/30#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/1-samuel/30#v26)</sup> And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the Lord;
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-samuel/30#v27)</sup> To them which were in Beth–el, and to them which were in south Ramoth, and to them which were in Jattir,
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-samuel/30#v28)</sup> And to them which were in Aroer, and to them which were in Siphmoth, and to them which were in Eshtemoa,
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-samuel/30#v29)</sup> And to them which were in Rachal, and to them which were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to them which were in the cities of the Kenites,
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-samuel/30#v30)</sup> And to them which were in Hormah, and to them which were in Chor–ashan, and to them which were in Athach,
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/1-samuel/30#v31)</sup> And to them which were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.

- When David came to Ziklag he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the Lord.
- The spoil went to them in Bethel, in south Ramoth, in Jattir, in Aroer, in Siphmoth, in Eshtemoa, in Rachal, in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, in the cities of the Kenites, in Hormah, in Chorashan, in Athach, in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.
- The chapter in sum: the Amalekites spoiled the city and took the families while the men were gone up with Achish; David sought the Lord first, was told to pursue and recover, and went down and recovered all; and when his men that fought did not want to share with the men that were too faint, David made everybody part alike.
